text:
maria: FYI traced a reproducible D2H stall during the new kvcache prefetch window test. nsys timeline shows a high-latency burst aligned with host-side page faults when prefetching > 1MB per request. attaching notes + commands. :thinking_face:

hugo: rough numbers? can you paste the nsys cmd and a tiny timeline snippet?

maria: nsys: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o prefetch_waveform --sample=none ./bin/serve --profile-mode`
Found the waveform: around 3:42 into the trace there are ~8 contiguous small peer transfers then a ~12ms gap where kernels wait for DMA completion. copying snippet from timeline view:
```
Time (ms) | Activity
3400      | kernel: matmul_small (cudaLaunch)
3401-3403 | cuMemcpyPeerAsync (nvlink) 0.9ms
3403-3405 | kernel: kv_prefetch
3405-3417 | WAIT (cuEvent/query) 12.2ms  <-- unexpected
3417-3419 | cuMemcpyAsync H2D (PCIe) 0.6ms
```

maria: The weird part: the wait correlates with the host doing page-in, not device-side work. perfetto stack shows page-fault handler on the host doing scatter-gather copies.

priya: are you allocating with pageable buffers in the kvcache path? we recently changed the prefetch size heuristic to avoid pinning everything.

maria: yes, prefetch path currently uses `malloc()` + async copy (no mlock). New heuristic tries to avoid pinning small user allocations to keep pinned pool small. reproduces only when prefetch window >= 1MB and request QPS > ~120.

hugo: smells like pageable stalls. nvlink peer copies are fine but when we fall back to PCIe H2D (host staging) page faults cause the kernel queues to back up. Do you have cupti counters or `cudaMemGetInfo` around the window?

maria: grabbed a short nvprof sample too: `nvprof --profile-from-start off --events gld_throughput,dram__sectors_read.sum ./bin/serve`
It shows spike in DRAM reads on host at same timestamps. Also `cuMemcpyAsync` durations jump from ~0.7ms -> 12ms when host does page-in.

sam: which commit changed prefetch sizing? I remember a batching tweak landed last week that switched us to (batch_size * 8KB) capped at 2MB.

maria: yep that was 3a7f9c2 (batching: prefetch heuristic). I bisected and saw regression introduced there. Before change we pinned windows <= 512KB, now we let them float up to 2MB and avoid mlock, so we hit more pageable hits.

priya: quick test: pin the prefetch buffers (temporary) and see if the 12ms gap disappears. If so, we can either revert to pin small windows or attempt a staged pin+copy pipeline.

maria: did that — pinning (cudaHostRegister) on prefetch buffer removes the host page-in gap. Numbers look clean: max transfer latency back to ~1ms, overall tail latency drops 9-12%.

hugo: good confirmation. We need to decide: prefer cost of additional pinned memory vs tail latency. For Dedicated customers we probably pin by default; for hosted maybe heuristic based on QPS or memory pressure.

priya: another angle: batching heuristic change also altered kernel selection order. For small batches we now schedule many tiny matmuls which produce more frequent small transfers (worse tail). Consider grouping into larger fused matmuls or increasing prefetch coalescing window when using pageable buffers.

sam: also check NVLink fallback path: when nvlink capacity is saturated we fallback to peer copy via host which would double-hit pageable behavior. Does trace show any fallback events?

maria: trace shows a few `cuIpcOpenMemHandle` fallbacks and explicit NVSwitch congestion markers. At ~3403 we had nvlink bandwidth at ~85% and then a burst caused scatter to host.

devops-bot: CI run https://ci.redwood/2026/serve/5234 showed increased p99 for prefetch test. (build 5234)

maria: next steps I'm proposing:
- revert prefetch heuristic to pin windows <= 512KB while we design adaptive policy (short-term)
- add runtime flag `--prefetch-pinning=auto|always|never` and default hosted->auto (pin under QPS threshold)
- add CI perf test (nsys sample) to catch this regression (fail if tail increases >5%)

hugo: +1. Can you open a quick PR with benchmark numbers and the nvprof/nsys snippets attached? include the perfetto screen grab.

maria: will do. PR will reference 3a7f9c2 and include a small reproducer script.

priya: one more ask: capture `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` traces too — there may be kernel-level prefetch calls we can leverage to move pages proactively.

maria: good call. I'll add a run with `cudaMemPrefetchAsync` path enabled and compare.

sam: nice debugging. also file a postmortem-lite in /incidents if this hits customers.

maria: noted. saving nsys export to s3://redwood-traces/prefetch-waveform/1905004321 and will link in PR. :thumbsup:
